Name: Jiajun Wu
description: Jiajun Wu leads a group studying physical scene understanding — building machines that see, reason about, and interact with the physical world. His current research topics span physical scene understanding, multimodal perception from visual, acoustic, and tactile signals, visual generation of the 4D physical world, visual reasoning via physical concept grounding, and robotics/embodied AI. Jiajunwu His recent MIT CSAIL talk was titled Understanding the Visual World Through Physical Intrinsics, focusing on controllable, action-conditioned 4D visual world reconstruction, generation, and interaction. MIT CSAIL This is arguably the single tightest fit. Wu is actively building AI that understands the physical world, which is your stated research mission. His group works at the intersection of perception, world modeling, and robotics — exactly where your JEPA SSL and LeDEEP depth work sits. Fit: Strongest alignment. World models, physical perception, multimodal learning, embodied AI. Physical Scene Understanding. Lab: https://jiajunwu.com

Name: Sergey Levine
description: Website: https://rail.eecs.berkeley.edu. The Robotic AI & Learning Lab (RAIL) at BAIR is headed by Sergey Levine. Berkeley Levine's group works on offline RL, self-supervised robot learning, and large-scale data-driven policies. Recent work from his lab includes DigiRL (autonomous RL for device-control agents) and AutoEval (autonomous evaluation of robot manipulation policies). UC Berkeley EECS His lab produced foundational work in offline RL (IQL, CQL) and is currently pushing on generalist robot policies. Your SSL + RL ablation work using contrastive and SIGReg losses maps directly onto the kinds of questions his lab cares about. Fit: SSL for robotics, RL with learned representations, sim-to-real transfer, self-supervised pretraining. RAIL Lab. Lab: https://rail.eecs.berkeley.edu

Name: Chelsea Finn
description: Chelsea Finn's lab IRIS studies intelligence through robotic interaction at scale, affiliated with SAIL and the ML Group. Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory She co-founded Physical Intelligence (Pi). Her recent work includes self-supervised and domain-agnostic masked autoencoders (ICLR 2024) and self-guided masked autoencoders for self-supervised learning. Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory She is a leading figure in meta-learning, self-supervised robot learning, and generalization. Fit: SSL for robotics, generalization, imitation learning, VLAs.IRIS Lab. Lab: https://irislab.stanford.edu

Name: Angjoo Kanazawa
description: Angjoo Kanazawa leads the Kanazawa AI Research (KAIR) lab under BAIR. Her research focuses on perceiving and understanding the dynamic 4D world from everyday photographs and video, and learning priors on the 4D world from image and video observations. UC Berkeley She has active work on video generation, 3D scene reconstruction, and view synthesis — directly relevant to your LeDEEP depth work and broader JEPA interest in learning structured world representations. Fit: 4D perception, visual world priors, self-supervised vision. KAIR Lab. Lab: https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~kanazawa/

Name: Yanjie Ze
description: Theme: Humanoid robotics, whole-body control, visuomotor learning. Ze is working on humanoid locomotion and manipulation, with recent work on the TWIST teleoperated whole-body imitation system (CoRL 2025) and Generalizable Humanoid Manipulation with 3D Diffusion Policies (IROS 2025 Oral). He interned at Amazon FAR (2025) and Figure AI's Helix team (2026). Strong intersection with your SSL + RL for humanoid locomotion work.

Name: Stephen Tian
description: Theme: Tactile sensing and contact-rich dexterous manipulation. Tian presented DexSkin — high-coverage conformable robotic skin for learning contact-rich manipulation — as an Oral at CoRL 2025. Also has a review paper on learning-based dynamics models in Science Robotics (2025). The dynamics + perception framing overlaps with your JEPA latent-world interest.

Name: Yunzhi Zhang
description: Theme: Visual representation learning, 3D scene understanding, generative world models. Zhang works on visual representations and visual generation — specifically the Scene Language work (programs, words, and embeddings as scene representations), and 3D congealing and multi-view consistency. Prior to Stanford she did research at BAIR under Abbeel and Pinto. Her work is a near-exact match to your representation learning research.

Name: Chen Geng
description: Theme: 4D vision, dynamic scene understanding, generative models for temporal world structure. Geng's CVPR 2025 paper is "Birth and Death of a Rose" — modeling the full 4D lifecycle of physical phenomena — and he has a related CVPR 2025 work on 4D vision and computer graphics. His focus on learning structured physical dynamics from video maps to your JEPA / world model interest.
papers: [Birth and Death of a Rose (CVPR 2025)](https://chen-geng.com/rose4d/) | [4D Vision (CVPR 2025)](https://chen-geng.com)

Name: Joy Hsu
description: Theme: Neuro-symbolic reasoning, concept grounding, compositional representation learning. Hsu is part of Wu's group, working on visual reasoning via physical concept grounding in the neuro-symbolic tradition (LEFT project — grounding language to structured perception). Her work sits at the junction of learning structured world representations and compositional reasoning — relevant to the "what JEPA should be learning" question in your research.

Name: Homer Walke
description: Theme: Large-scale robot learning, VLAs, dataset collection. Walke led BridgeData V2 (CoRL 2023), a large-scale robot learning dataset, and contributed to the π0.5 Vision-Language-Action model (CoRL 2025). He also works on autonomous improvement of instruction-following via foundation models. Direct connection to data-driven generalist robotics — relevant to your interests in SSL for real-world robot generalization.

Name: Seohong Park
description: Theme: Scalable offline RL, goal-conditioned RL, offline-to-online learning. Park's driving research question is whether RL is truly scalable. He introduced OGBench, a new benchmark for offline goal-conditioned RL, and Flow Q-Learning (FQL), which uses flow matching for offline RL policies. His work on offline RL scalability with expressive objectives is a strong parallel to your contrastive vs. SIGReg loss experiments.

Name: Kevin Frans
description: Theme: Deep learning theory, self-improving systems, scalable RL, generative modeling. Frans's interests are in understanding deep learning and scalable self-improving systems, with prior work in RL and generative modeling. He previously spent time at OpenAI on the RL team. Recent work includes one-step diffusion via shortcut models and an analysis of matrix-whitening optimizers (SPlus) for training stability.
papers: [Diffusion Guidance as Policy Improvement (arXiv)](https://kvfrans.com/) | [What Really Matters in Matrix-Whitening Optimizers (2025)](https://kvfrans.com/)

Name: Qiyang (Colin) Li
description: Theme: Generative models for RL, offline + online exploration. Li's research focuses on leveraging expressive generative models to improve RL algorithms for both offline learning and online exploration. His framing — generative models as a structural tool for RL, not just data augmentation — overlaps with the representational questions in your contrastive SSL + RL work.
papers: [ICML 2025 work with Frans & Levine](https://colinqiyangli.github.io/) | [Generative model-based RL exploration](https://colinqiyangli.github.io/)

Name: Vivek Myers
description: Theme: RL, human-AI interaction, robot goal specification. Myers works on reinforcement learning, human-AI interaction, and robotics with NDSEG fellowship support. His work on semi-supervised language interfaces for robot control (CoRL 2023) is directly relevant if you're thinking about how to ground SSL representations in language-conditioned tasks.
papers: [Goal Representations for Instruction Following (CoRL 2023)](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~vmyers/) | [Stabilizing Contrastive RL (ICLR 2024 Spotlight)](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~vmyers/)

Name: Karl Pertsch
description: Theme: Generalist robot policies, VLA evaluation, large-scale robot data. Pertsch co-led OpenVLA (CoRL 2024), an open-source Vision-Language-Action model, and RoboArena (2025), a distributed real-world evaluation system for generalist robot policies. The most senior lab member — a great entry point for discussing VLA-related research.

Name: Lucy Shi
description: Theme: Robot learning from corrections and human feedback, manipulation. Shi co-authored "Yell At Your Robot" (RSS 2024), studying how robots can improve on-the-fly from language corrections during deployment. She also contributed to Mobile ALOHA's bimanual mobile manipulation experiments. Her work on interactive, feedback-driven robot learning is at the frontier of data-efficient policy improvement.

Name: Anikait Singh
description: Theme: RL for LLMs, preference optimization, test-time reasoning. Singh works on preference fine-tuning for LLMs, scalable RL for reasoning, and cognitive behaviors for self-improving reasoners. Recent works include RLAD (training LLMs to discover abstractions) and Big-Math (a large-scale RL math dataset), both from 2025. Slightly less robotics-focused, but directly relevant if you want to discuss RL + SSL for language-grounded agents.

Name: Jonathan Yang
description: Theme: Robot manipulation, policy generalization across morphologies. Yang works on policy mobilization and robot manipulation generalization, with a recent CoRL 2025 paper on policy mobilization for mobile manipulation. His work on generalizing visuomotor policies across different robot embodiments is relevant to your VLA + SSL work. (Email not listed in source.)

Name: Moo Jin Kim
description: Theme: VLAs, open-source robot foundation models. Kim is a primary author on OpenVLA, the open-source VLA model that achieved state-of-the-art performance on robot manipulation benchmarks (CoRL 2024). If your angle is SSL pretraining feeding into VLA-style policies, he's the most natural PhD-level contact in the lab.

Name: Hongsuk Choi
description: Theme: Humanoid control from video, 4D human-scene reconstruction. Choi is a co-first author on VideoMimic (CoRL 2025, Best Student Paper Award) — a system that reconstructs 3D environments and human motion from single-camera videos for humanoid imitation learning. He also co-authored a CVPR 2025 Highlight on reconstructing people, places, and cameras. This is a direct intersection of visual perception and humanoid robot control, which maps well onto your depth + SSL + RL stack.
papers: [VideoMimic (CoRL 2025 Best Student Paper)](https://hongsukchoi.github.io/) | [Reconstructing People, Places, Cameras (CVPR 2025)](https://hongsukchoi.github.io/)

Name: Chung Min Kim
description: Theme: Robot kinematics, kinematic optimization tools, contact-aware manipulation. Kim co-led PyRoki (IROS 2025), a modular, cross-platform toolkit for robot kinematic optimization, supporting inverse kinematics, trajectory optimization, and motion retargeting across CPU/GPU/TPU. Also contributed to VideoMimic and Eye, Robot. (Email not listed in source.)

Name: Brent Yi
description: Theme: Egocentric body estimation, camera-relative pose, 3D world reconstruction. Yi led EgoAllo (CVPR 2025), which estimates body and hand motion in an ego-sensed world using egocentric SLAM poses and a conditional diffusion model, with a novel parameterization for spatial and temporal invariance. His work on learning geometry-aware representations from egocentric video is directly relevant to your depth + SSL interest. (Email not listed in source.)

Name: David McAllister
description: Theme: Flow-based RL, generative policies, score distillation. McAllister introduced Flow Policy Optimization (FPO, arXiv 2025), an on-policy RL algorithm that integrates flow matching into the policy gradient framework, enabling multimodal action distributions without recursive backpropagation. Also contributed to VideoMimic. The combination of generative models and RL connects directly to your contrastive + generative model ablation work. (Email not listed in source.)

Name: Justin Kerr
description: Theme: Perception-action loops, active vision for robot manipulation. Kerr co-led "Eye, Robot" (CoRL 2025) — studying how to jointly learn to look and act using a BC-RL perception-action loop — and earlier "Robot See Robot Do" (CoRL 2024), which reconstructs articulated object manipulation from monocular 4D video for robot imitation. (Email not listed in source.)
